answer:
**Sí — la relación SES → probabilidad de completar un BA está modulada por la línea racial.** La pendiente positiva de SES es significativamente más pronunciada en el grupo Black (y en dirección consistente en el grupo Hispanic) que en el grupo White.

En un modelo logístico de `BA DEGREE COMPLETED ~ SES(continuo, por +1 SD) × RACE (ref = White)`, cada +1 SD de SES multiplica las odds de completar el grado por ≈1.18 en Whites (p=.031), ≈1.65 en Hispanics (p=.013) y ≈2.07 en Blacks (p<.001). La interacción SES×Black tiene OR = 1.76 (IC95% 1.21–2.55, p=.003) y el test conjunto de la interacción SES×RACE es significativo (razón de verosimilitud p=.008; Wald p=.006): hay **heterogeneidad racial estadísticamente significativa del efecto SES**.

La moderación es **robusta al controlar por capacidad cognitiva** (modelo de efecto directo con ASVAB+percentile: SES×Black OR 1.75, p=.006) pero **se atenúa parcialmente al controlar por family size** (test conjunto p=.28 tras añadir sex+family size), lo que indica que parte de la moderación se explica por las diferencias de family size entre razas.

Matiz clave: los Whites tienen mayor tasa de completación a **todos** los niveles de SES (base ≈3.5% vs ≈1.3–1.4% en Black/Hispanic), así que la "ventaja" de un SES alto se concentra en los grupos Black e Hispanic, aunque su completación absoluta siga siendo menor.

*(Limitaciones: la completación de BA es un resultado raro —236/8773 = 2.69%— y los estratos Black/Hispanic tienen solo 19–28 eventos, por lo que las interacciones tienen IC anchos y potencia limitada; el término Hispanic×SES no es significativo por sí solo.)*

payload.hypothesis: Yes — the SES -> bachelor's-degree-completion relationship is modulated by race. The positive SES slope is significantly steeper for Black respondents (and directionally for Hispanic respondents) than for White respondents. In a logistic model of BA completion on SES (continuous, per +1 SD) x race (reference = White), each +1 SD of SES multiplies the odds of degree completion by ~1.18 in Whites (p=.031), ~1.65 in Hispanics (p=.013) and ~2.07 in Blacks (p<.001); the Black x SES interaction OR is 1.76 (95% CI 1.21-2.55, p=.003) and the joint SES x race interaction test is significant (likelihood-ratio p=.008; Wald p=.006), i.e., there is statistically significant racial heterogeneity of the SES effect. The moderation is robust to adjusting for cognitive ability (direct-effect model with ASVAB + class percentile: Black x SES OR 1.75, p=.006) but is partly explained by family size (joint interaction p=.28 after adding sex + family size). Whites nonetheless have higher completion at every SES level (base rate ~3.5% vs ~1.3-1.4% for Black/Hispanic), so the benefit of higher SES is concentrated in the Black and Hispanic groups even though their absolute completion remains lower. Caveats: BA completion is rare (236/8773 = 2.7%) and Black/Hispanic strata have only 19-28 events, so interaction estimates have wide CIs and limited power; the Hispanic x SES term is not individually significant.
payload.workflow: Loaded data/nls_ses_processed.csv (N=8773, 0 missing), dropped the spurious row-index column, standardized SES/ASVAB/percentile to z-scores, and one-hot encoded SAMPLE_RACE with reference = White. M1 (total effect): logistic BA ~ SES_z * RACE, no ability covariates; homogeneity of effect tested with a likelihood-ratio test (full vs main-effects, df=2) plus a joint Wald test of the two SES x race interaction terms (continuous-exposure analogue of Breslow-Day). Stratification: per-race logistic SES slope with 95% CI, a crosstab of BA rate by race x SES tercile reporting events/n, and predicted-probability curves vs SES by race (exported to artifacts/pred_prob_curves_M1.csv since matplotlib was unavailable). M2 added SAMPLE_SEX and FAMILY SIZE; M3 added ASVAB_z and PERCENTILE_z as a direct-effect/sensitivity analysis. Firth bias-reduced logistic (implemented manually, no external package) was run as a cross-check; standard MLE converged for all models so it was reported as primary. All code and a numeric summary are saved under artifacts/.
